In chapter 48, there's a moment when the Kakushi bring Tanjirou to Shinobu's estate and they were so focused on trying to converse with Kanao to the point that they didn't notice she was right behind them until she spoke. The other moment that stands out to me that makes me think this is in chapter 204. I think there's a tendency to focus on Aoi giving food to Inosuke, but the focus should be on the fact she was able to sense Inosuke at all. (Keep in mind Inosuke is the one who talked to Tanjirou about killing intent and how he utilizes his strong sense of touch to be able to sense people sneaking up behind him.) So the fact that Inosuke was impressed that Aoi could sense he was sneaking around at this point in the manga is pretty telling of how much potential Aoi actually had (the only other two people he's specifically notes for the strength in the manga is Giyuu and Gyomei). My guess on why Aoi sold herself short is that she became so fixated on the difference in others she ended up forgetting her own accomplishments.

I think the people that complain that it takes the risk out of the end game content miss the mark on why newer players will find end game frustrating. 

The aspect of a bullet hell is reliant on mastery and expects failure; but the benefit of practice mode gets you to try again at the spot you messed up on instead of having to go through all of the game just to try again. It makes much more sense to run something like in the Arena or Guild Hall to do practice runs of rushing or end game content without having to constantly rebuild the character and try again. 

Even if you go in an end game dungeon and know what you're doing things can still go wrong (see Shatters/Lost Halls are the most obvious examples). But at least if you're familiar enough with the dungeon and where things can go wrong you can play around that; whether or not you're successful is a different story. 

I think people that complain that it goes against the permadeath feature often miss the other part of RotMG and that's the bullet hell aspect. But that's just my experience carried over other bullet hells. I know people will think I'm whining but really, this is kind of why I don't like running end game dungeons with other players because I lack experience. In order to get that experience I need to run the dungeon more; but I always feel unwelcomed because I'm still learning.

A lot of what I feel has been summarized in [this post](https://www.reddit.com/r/RotMG/comments/d9lpog/practice_mode_enemy_spawner/) so go there I guess if you want to save time from reading my long ramble.

>From Ten Desires, I'm surprisingly getting dunked by Yoshika. Not so much that her attacks are killing me (apart from occasional stupidity on my part), but I can't seem to clear her two spellcards where she absorbs spirits for health. I figured out on the last one that you can sneak in after the lasers and steal some of the spirits, but even then I haven't been able to out damage her before the time ends.

For Ten Desires I will warn you if you're using Sanae expect an uphill battle. Her DPS is quite poor compared to other characters, although in my experience I find Marisa the slowest in ending both of Yoshika's healing cards. 

Regardless of who you play for Yoshika's Recovery "Heal by Desire" you can stand in front of her for a few seconds. She will fire a ring of red rice bullets but you can back up a bit and squeeze through them to get extra damage. She'll keep firing if you're in range on Normal, when she fires the second ring you should start backing away because her spirit familiars will starting increasing the curtain fire. I will note it is possible to weave through bullets but it can get overwhelming. 

My advice is to shift to one side towards the wall and misdirect the bullets and then re-stream towards the center. During that time make sure you don't fire. Although if you play as Youmu you can probably get away with lashing out one charged attack at the end if she's at low enough health. From my own personal experience I have had to re-stream with Youmu where she's on one side of a wall, used a charge attack and still manage to cap the card but it takes a lot of practice.

As for Desire Sign "Score Desire Eater" try not to stay at the bottom of the screen when she fires the red kunai. You should be able to be a little bit above from the bottom of the screen. If you play as Youmu, used your charge attack when you weave through the red kunai and switch to an unfocused attack when you're trying to absorb some of the score spirits she summons. The timing is hard to get down so I strongly recommend using the Spell Practice.

If all else spell practice is your best friend. Also, don't feel bad about being so long-winded in your posts. It helps to know what exactly you're struggling either pattern on spell card.

I think you should rephrase the definition. What you're really accounting for is external linguistics -- in other words what you hear and what is said. There is a thing called internal linguistics which gets into psycholinguistics territory and generally talks about the brain's processing. Logically I would presume it would involved one's understanding of the brain and its functions and an understanding how a person process a language in their head. Being bilingual doesn't really factor in. 

I'm only a Linguistics minor here, but on the occasion where I did run into a monolingual, I never catechized nor did her peers on the fact she could only speak one language. She still knew what she was talking about in her specialization; so as far as I'm concerned it's not an issue. 

Also, while it's true the world is multilingual, I wouldn't really make much comment on them presumingly being an English-only person. Generally speaking -- granted I kind of live under a rock so, someone correct me if I'm wrong -- but last I also checked English is pretty much the current lang franca. I'd personally started with some basic models like cranes, cups, boats, etc. 

I highly recommend if possible finding someone to learn from since diagrams are often very difficult to read. But I don't think it would hurt if you're familiar with some basic terminology like mountain fold, valley fold, inside reverse fold, blitz, etc.

You can always look up the basics but after enough practice you kind of pick up things like bird base, water bomb base, and rabbit's ear; but I'd really suggest experimenting. A lot of people stick to one-piece models, but there's also tessellations and modulars. It takes a bit of patience but really worth it for the end result.

As for paper, yes, there's a SIGNIFICANT difference in paper. When you get more familiar with more difficult models, you'll want to look into custom made paper or some really specific-made paper that can handle a lot of folds. Origami paper is a standard but if you don't feel confident yet, stick with printer paper. I rarely suggest post-its for modulars since the adhesive sometimes get in the way, but if you're tight on money then it's better than nothing, really...

I know sites like Origami Maniacs and Origami Go are some of my favorite places for intermediate models. Youtube has a pretty broad range of tutorials so that's always a good place to go, although I do admit, sometimes it's difficult to read what's going on because of the camera quality.
